step1_summary.chief_complaint: Difficulty breathing after a recent wasp/bee sting
symptoms: Onset: A few minutes ago following an insect sting
Difficulty breathing - mild, not acute at the time of consultation
Rash and slight redness on right arm at sting site
Sensation of swelling in right side of lips, but no visible swelling
No prior medication taken yet (e.g., antihistamines)
step1_summary.past_medical_history: History of eczema, no known history of anaphylaxis or severe allergies
step1_summary.medications/allergies: Allergic to penicillin, not on any medications currently
step1_summary.family/social_history: No significant family history of acute allergic reactions or illnesses; works as a computer scientist; lives alone; owns a cat
vital_signs/exam_findings: Normal breathing and speech during assessment
No visible lip swelling or airway compromise
Rash at sting site is slightly red with a puncture mark, no significant swelling
No signs of stridor or distress

V: Allergic angioedema with airway edema concern - possible vascular leakage in lips/tongue though no signs present now
I: Local cellulitis at sting site - possible bacterial infection if redness/spread worsens
D: Atopic dermatitis flare (eczema) - prior history, may complicate reaction
I2: Drug allergy (penicillin noted but not related to current symptoms)
A: Acute hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis to insect sting - localised allergic reaction currently without systemic involvement
T: Local tissue injury from insect sting causing inflammatory reaction

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Localized allergic reaction to wasp/bee sting
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient presents shortly after wasp/bee sting with local rash and mild symptoms consistent with a normal localized allergic reaction; no systemic features of anaphylaxis noted.
supporting_evidence: Recent wasp/bee sting
Local rash and redness at sting site with puncture mark
No significant swelling or respiratory distress
Symptoms started minutes ago; current mild presentation
opposing_evidence: Patient reports feeling of swelling in lip and tongue weirdness, but no objective swelling seen

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient reports difficulty breathing and lip/tongue symptoms shortly after sting, which could indicate early systemic allergic reaction; however, no objective airway compromise or severe symptoms during assessment make this less likely currently.
supporting_evidence: Difficulty breathing reported (though mild and not present at time of exam)
Sensation of swelling in lips and tongue
Recent insect sting
opposing_evidence: No history of severe allergies or previous anaphylaxis

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Local cellulitis or soft tissue infection at sting site
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Redness and rash present; possible early infection but no warmth, spreading redness or systemic signs; usually develops after longer duration than a few minutes.
supporting_evidence: Redness and rash over sting site
opposing_evidence: Onset too recent (minutes) for typical cellulitis

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient has history of occasional anxiety and is worried about worsening symptoms; subjective breathing difficulty could be anxiety driven rather than true airway compromise.
supporting_evidence: History of occasional anxiety
Patient describes feeling anxious about breathing
opposing_evidence: Some physical signs attributable to local sting reaction
Sensation of lip/tongue swelling is subjective
